Provenance columns in posterior tables

Source: R/provenance.R
posterior_provenance.Rd

Posterior tables retain the existing estimate and identifier columns and add ordinary columns describing how the result was computed. These columns are included in default reports and CSV exports; compact reports omit most of them. Unknown or inapplicable values are typed NA.

Columns

  • analysis_type: response, hypothesis, joint hypothesis, simultaneous band, representative selection, response timing, or diagnostic analysis.

  • interval_probability and interval_method: the mass and construction of intervals actually reported, equal_tailed or empirical_sup_norm.

  • scale_by, scale_var, and scale_factor: response normalisation. A shock_sd response is divided by the reported sample standard deviation.

  • units: known units such as FEVD percentages or response-timing periods; economic units are left unknown when they cannot be recovered.

  • source_package and source_version: the upstream package used for the current computation. They do not reconstruct estimation software history.

  • n_draws: number of posterior draws used for the result.

  • draw_id: original draw labels in draw-level tables. The integer draw column retains positional indexing.

  • selected_draw_id: original label of a representative draw; draw_index remains its positional index.

Existing object_type, draws, and compare attributes remain supported. Legacy tables without provenance columns can still be plotted when their analysis is unambiguous from the existing columns and attributes.

See also

tidy_irf(), report_table(), write_bsvar_csv()
